title: Dotted-path lookup in nested dicts
description: Implement get_path(data, path, default). Walk a dotted path through nested dicts and return the value found. data must be a dict (else TypeError). path must be a str (else TypeError); an empty path or any empty segment (leading, trailing, or doubled dots) raises ValueError. At each step the current value must be a dict (else TypeError). If a segment is missing: return default when one was passed, otherwise raise KeyError naming the missing segment. Passing default=None explicitly is valid and distinct from omitting it. A stored value of None is a real value and is returned, not treated as missing. Segments are matched exactly; spaces are not trimmed.
invariants: The sentinel distinguishes 'no default passed' (KeyError on a missing segment) from default=None (returns None on a missing segment).
Traversing into a non-dict value (path 'a.b' where data['a'] is 5) raises TypeError.
Split is on '.'; spaces are not trimmed and segments are matched exactly.
Empty path and empty segments ('', '.a', 'a.', 'a..b') are ValueError.
The found value is returned unchanged whatever its type, including None.
